title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.130-132). Grothendieck attaches to a Riemann surface X the canonical structures of its uniformization, already set out on the previous page:
(a) a P^1-bundle P_X = X~ x_{pi1} P^1;
(b) a flat connection c_X on it;
(c) a section sigma (the developing map), nowhere stationary;
(d) a formal isomorphism, compatible with connections, between the completion of P_X along sigma and the completion of X_X = X x X along the diagonal Delta_X.
He asks which of these are algebraic when X is algebraic. The next page answers for (a)-(c): P = P(E) with E = J/J^3 (x) omega^{-1}, the canonical extension 0 -> omega -> E -> O -> 0 coming from second-order jets. This is an algebraic description of the indigenous bundle (PGL_2-oper) that avoids choosing a square root of omega.

This page. Suppose such algebraic data (P_X, c_X, sigma) are given on an algebraic curve X/C. How do we recover the analytic uniformization from them? Concretely, we must build an open subset X~ of (P_X)^an and a map p_X: X~ -> (X_X)^an. On each fibre this map is the universal covering P^1_x ⊃ disc -> X, sending sigma to the diagonal. We already have the formal isomorphism (d); the task is to prolong it. Three cases, which are exactly the elliptic / parabolic / hyperbolic trichotomy:
1) X = P^1. The prolongation is an isomorphism P_X ≅ X_X, and it is algebraic.
2) Parabolic cases: X ≅ A^1, G_m, or an elliptic curve. There is a horizontal section sigma' (the monodromy-fixed point at infinity). Then X~ := P_X^an minus sigma'(X^an) maps to (X_X)^an as a fibrewise covering sending sigma to Delta_X. It is an isomorphism iff X is simply connected and non-proper, i.e. X ≅ A^1. In that case p_X is itself algebraic. He asks for a purely algebraic description of sigma' in terms of (P_X, c_X, sigma).
3) Hyperbolic case. X~ is an open subset of P_X^an whose fibres are discs. These discs are characterised as the maximal domains of existence of the analytic continuation of the formal maps f^_x : (P^1_x)^an -> X^an, given at each x by the formal isomorphism (d). The disc boundary is cut out by the 'imaginary section' sigma-bar of the previous page. The lower left margin seems to restate this for case 2°/3° (discs Delta ⊂ C in the fibres).

So the page frames uniformization as: an algebraic indigenous bundle with its canonical section, plus an analytic-continuation datum that is not algebraic in general.
errors: Mathematically the case analysis is correct. Case 2 lists exactly the parabolic curves (A^1, G_m, elliptic curves). The covering is an isomorphism exactly for A^1, and p_X is then algebraic (the identity-type map P^1 minus a point = A^1).
The machine transcription garbles the formula in 2°. The removed set is sigma'^an(X^an), the image of the horizontal section, not 'pi^{-1 an}(X^an)'.

Gap, not error: the question of an algebraic description of the hyperbolic disc boundary (sigma-bar) is left open. The real-analytic, non-algebraic nature of sigma-bar shows that a purely algebraic description cannot exist in that case.

Gap, not error: the algebraic data (P, c, sigma) on the next page do not single out the uniformizing connection among all projective structures. That is the transcendental accessory-parameter problem, not addressed here.

ideas.what: Uniformization of a Riemann surface encoded as a flat P^1-bundle with a nowhere-stationary section (developing map), plus a formal isomorphism with the completion of X x X along the diagonal
ideas.modern_name: indigenous bundle / projective structure / PGL_2-oper with developing map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1967) for indigenous bundles; Beilinson-Drinfeld for opers; Mochizuki for the p-adic theory

ideas.what: Trichotomy P^1 / parabolic (A^1, G_m, elliptic) / hyperbolic read off from the geometry of the developing image. In the parabolic case there is a horizontal section at infinity and X~ = P minus that section covers X x X; the map is algebraic exactly for A^1
ideas.modern_name: elliptic/parabolic/hyperbolic uniformization via affine vs Fuchsian projective structures

ideas.what: Uniformizing discs characterised as the maximal domains of existence of the analytic continuation of the formal inverse map f^_x: P^1_x -> X determined by the formal identification of the completion along sigma with the completion of X x X along the diagonal
ideas.modern_name: inverse of the developing map / Schwarz-type analytic continuation
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; formal-groupoid phrasing related to Deligne's and Katz's work on connections

ideas.what: Question whether the extra uniformization data (horizontal section sigma', or p_X) admit a purely algebraic description
ideas.modern_name: algebraicity of uniformization; accessory parameter problem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Poincaré/Klein (accessory parameters); Ihara (1974) and Mochizuki (1996) for arithmetic versions

missed.claim: Around 1972 Grothendieck formulates an algebraic theory of uniformization via indigenous bundles: (P, c, sigma) with P = P(J/J^3 (x) omega^{-1}) on the adjacent page. It sits in the same dossier as notes on the Cartier operator and Gauss-Manin connections. This anticipates the framework of Ihara's Schwarzian equations in characteristic p and of Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory (indigenous bundles, p-curvature / dormant opers). Neither credits Grothendieck, and the page itself contains no p-adic content.
missed.quote: A-t-on une description purement algébrique de σ' ... Et de p_X dans le cas où c'est un iso analytique i.e. X ≃ E^1_C - alors p_X est lui-même algébrique !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents an early Grothendieck interest in the algebraic structure of uniformization, predating the Esquisse's Teichmüller program. The jet description of the oper bundle without a choice of theta-characteristic is a clean formulation that is natural over arbitrary bases of characteristic 0.

missed.claim: The question of algebraically describing the analytic part of uniformization (sigma' in the parabolic case, the disc boundary in the hyperbolic case) is posed and not resolved. In the parabolic case it plausibly has an algebraic answer (the monodromy-fixed horizontal section). In the hyperbolic case it cannot have one.
missed.quote: Question A-t-on une description purement algébrique de σ' (... des P_X, c_X, σ_X) ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is essentially the known transcendence of accessory parameters. It is not new mathematically, but it shows how Grothendieck separated the algebraic from the transcendental parts of uniformization.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (projective structures, the uniformization trichotomy, the developing map as analytic continuation of a formal isomorphism) is classical. What is notable is the historical fact: around 1972 Grothendieck was formulating uniformization algebraically via indigenous bundles with a canonical jet-theoretic description, in a dossier also about the Cartier operator. This foreshadows Ihara and Mochizuki without appearing in his published texts. No new theorem is on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'Quand on a de telles données algébriques sur courbe algébrique X/C, comment reconstruire la situation analytique du th. en termes de celles-ci ?' rather than 'des familles de courbes algébriques ... uniformisations des fibres'.
'Il on a déjà un bon fermé [?] de)' should probably read 'Or on a déjà un bon iso formel d), et celui-ci pourrait se prolonger, suivant les cas'.

In 2°: 'Un hom X~ =df P_X^an − σ'^an(X^an) → (X_X)^an, si σ' est une section horizontale (unique donc déterminée) de P_X sur X, faisant de X~ un rev. de (X_X)^an, et transformant σ en Δ_X'. The transcription's 'π^{-1 an}' should be σ'^an, and 'induisant disque déterminé' is likely 'unique donc déterminée'.
'(Cas pas un iso ...)' should probably read '(Cas p est un iso ssi X ≃ E^1_C i.e. X simplement connexe non propre)'.
'X ≃ E^1_C, [?] C, ou X courbe elliptique' should probably read 'X ≃ E^1_C, G_{m,C}, ou X courbe elliptique'.
'(ou de [?] qui [?] ou aux [?] des P_X, ε_X, p_X)' should probably read '(en supposant qu'on ait les données P_X, c_X, σ_X)'.
In 3°: 'un ouvert X~ (dont les fibres sont des disques) de P_X^an'. The superscript in f^_x is likely (P^1_x)^an_formal or similar, mapping to X^an.
